content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Git Basics, Branching, and Merging Tutorial"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial provides a basic introduction to Git, covering essential commands, branching strategies, and merging techniques. Git is a distributed version control system that allows you to track changes to your code, collaborate with others, and revert to previous versions if needed."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"Basic Git Commands"},{"order":4,"type":"subheading","text":"Initializing a Repository"},{"order":5,"type":"paragraph","text":"To start using Git in a project, you need to initialize a repository. Navigate to your project directory in the terminal and run the following command:"},{"order":6,"type":"code","text":"git init"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"This command creates a new .git subdirectory in your project, which contains all the necessary repository metadata."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Adding and Committing Changes"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before committing changes, you need to stage them using the 'git add' command. To add all modified files, use:"},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"git add ."},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"To add a specific file, use:"},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"git add <file_name>"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once the changes are staged, you can commit them with a descriptive message:"},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"git commit -m \"Your commit message here\""},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Checking the Status"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"To check the status of your repository, use the following command:"},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"git status"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"This command shows you which files have been modified, staged, or are untracked."},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Viewing the Commit History"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"To view the commit history, use the following command:"},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"git log"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"This command displays a list of commits, including their authors, dates, and messages."},{"order":23,"type":"heading","text":"Branching"},{"order":24,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating a Branch"},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"Branches allow you to work on new features or bug fixes in isolation. To create a new branch, use the following command:"},{"order":26,"type":"code","text":"git branch <branch_name>"},{"order":27,"type":"subheading","text":"Switching Branches"},{"order":28,"type":"paragraph","text":"To switch to a different branch, use the following command:"},{"order":29,"type":"code","text":"git checkout <branch_name>"},{"order":30,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can also create and switch to a new branch in one step using:"},{"order":31,"type":"code","text":"git checkout -b <branch_name>"},{"order":32,"type":"subheading","text":"Listing Branches"},{"order":33,"type":"paragraph","text":"To list all branches in your repository, use the following command:"},{"order":34,"type":"code","text":"git branch"},{"order":35,"type":"heading","text":"Merging"},{"order":36,"type":"subheading","text":"Merging Branches"},{"order":37,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once you've completed your work on a branch, you can merge it back into the main branch (usually 'main' or 'master'). First, switch to the target branch:"},{"order":38,"type":"code","text":"git checkout main"},{"order":39,"type":"paragraph","text":"Then, merge the other branch into the current branch:"},{"order":40,"type":"code","text":"git merge <branch_name>"},{"order":41,"type":"paragraph","text":"If there are no conflicts, Git will automatically merge the changes. If there are conflicts, you'll need to resolve them manually by editing the affected files."},{"order":42,"type":"subheading","text":"Resolving Conflicts"},{"order":43,"type":"paragraph","text":"When conflicts occur, Git will mark the conflicting sections in the affected files. You'll need to edit these files to choose which changes to keep. After resolving the conflicts, stage the changes and commit them:"},{"order":44,"type":"code","text":"git add <file_name>\ngit commit -m \"Resolved merge conflicts\""},{"order":45,"type":"subheading","text":"Deleting a Branch"},{"order":46,"type":"paragraph","text":"After merging a branch, you can delete it using the following command:"},{"order":47,"type":"code","text":"git branch -d <branch_name>"},{"order":48,"type":"paragraph","text":"If the branch has not been merged, you can force delete it using:"},{"order":49,"type":"code","text":"git branch -D <branch_name>"},{"order":50,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial covers the basic Git commands, branching, and merging. There are many other advanced features in Git, such as rebasing, stashing, and remote repositories, which you can explore further as you become more comfortable with the basics."}]
